text: Sanborn's double and triple matrixes: write in rows, copy out down the columns, up to three times, then use the table. Every triple with all widths up to 24 was done (0134); here every triple with a grid 25 to 96 wide.

105,548,253 distinct routes, each with a repeating key of 1-26 on the sculpture's tables after or before, against the 24 known letters and ten scrambled copies, in compiled code checked against Python.
Shortest key that fits K4: 18 after the stages, 24 before; copies 19 and 17. K4 above every copy in 3 of 52 cells, a copy 0-3: chance.
